challenge.better_approach: Considered rebasing the ladder by hand (refused: rung 4 is the only door), and one admitting ticket per proof (refused by the measurement: two tickets moved import_sieve's proof under one open ladder, so no single id can carry it). A union of ids is the smallest change that matches what happened.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That bounds.in is cast-time and not widened after the build; a ticket's later edits ride the artifact door and are journaled, so a widened bounds.in is visible, but this gate does not check when it was written.
challenge.prior_art: Grepped CairnCommons/tickets for 'rung 4': e8be83a46ea9 (rung by ticket kind, x = PROVES names it), 6eb235ee813d (teeth of a renamed proof), 37ddc47686c2 (an answered question lifts it), 2dd69b2ba087 (plain seal asks the same gate), 4d9115eb04cd (the ruled ladder). None reads bounds.in or takes more than one id.
challenge.real_collision: e8be83a46ea9's x rule says PROVES names it. This widens x, it does not contradict it: PROVES says which clause a proof tests, bounds.in says which files a ticket is licensed to change, and rung 4's why (outline 19.14.8.2-3) is a recorded reason for the change, which both are. A distinction to record, not a collision.

answers.falsifier: 1: two code-seams that both declare the proof in bounds.in are admitted together; 2: either alone is refused naming the uncovered ticket; 3: a code-seam naming the proof in neither PROVES nor bounds.in is refused; 4: a removed tooth no ticket names is refused.
answers.from_idea: none, because the orchestrator's adjudication of the measured q47 refusal on cairn/tools/import_sieve/proofs/test_import_sieve.py bore it directly; the code it changes is cairn/devices/tester/reseal.py
answers.how: In cairn/devices/tester/reseal.py: _ticket_refusal's rung x admits a code-seam whose bounds.in names the proof as well as one whose PROVES names it; rung4_refusal splits a comma-separated --ruling into ticket ids, every id must admit and the proof text must name each; the removed-teeth check runs once over the union (a removed tooth is admitted if the proof names it). Red-first proof with scratch tickets and a scratch git proof.
answers.traces_to: Law 4 (rung 4 is the physics for 'a proof's assertions move only under a recorded reason') and Law 1 (a cast-time bounds.in is that reason already recorded; asking for it again re-derives the settled).
answers.what: Rung 4 admits a proof's moved bytes when every code-seam that moved them declared the proof in its cast-time bounds.in, and admits several such tickets together as one union.

bullets.text: q47 refused import_sieve's seal at rung 4: dd79ed8a1ece and 149b9a1ab9c4 both moved the proof under one ladder, and one id cannot admit two tickets' changes.
A code-seam's bounds.in naming the proof is a recorded reason for moving it, so x now reads it as well as PROVES.
